public_rationale: Anthropic's contemporary engineering reports describe incomplete work, inadequate testing, and a need for operator involvement or additional scaffolding. These make the warning about one-prompt completeness plausible. They do not directly establish the categorical Salesforce claim. The searches also did not locate a qualifying success. Absence of such a demonstration is insufficient to score incapability as supported.
limitations: The available technical evidence concerns other application types or tasks.
A simple CRM prototype and a complete operating competitor are materially different thresholds.
Later demonstrations cannot be applied to the earlier capability window.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Claude Code is not capable of building a Salesforce competitor from a prompt.

statement.excerpt: Let's start with the simplest, and least-technical way of putting it: even in the best-case scenario, you do not just type "Build Be A Salesforce Competitor" and it erupts, fully-formed, from your Terminal window. It is not capable of building it, but even if it were, it would need to actually be on a cloud hosting platform, and have all manner of actual customer data entered into it.

from_speaker: you do not just type "Build Be A Salesforce Competitor"
It is not capable of building it
our_interpretation: Read the claim as denying that one broad prompt produces a complete, operationally usable Salesforce competitor.
A plausible competing CRM need not reproduce every Salesforce product, but must offer usable core CRM workflows, persistent data, access control, and a practical way to operate it.
Allow ordinary preconfigured tools and infrastructure, while distinguishing their existence from manual engineering after the prompt.
The surrounding discussion concerns late-2025 and early-2026 capabilities. Use that pre-publication capability window, rather than later versions.
The hosting and customer-data remarks clarify the intended completeness standard; they are not treated as a universal claim that all CRM software must use public-cloud hosting.
criteria.support_condition: Direct contemporary testing and technical evidence establish that a single broad prompt cannot deliver a usable CRM competitor without substantive additional human engineering or setup.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducible contemporary trial shows one broad prompt producing a functioning, deployable CRM competitor, with its core workflows and operational requirements verified and interventions disclosed.
